title: Graph Bottlenecked Social Recommendation

problem.claim: Observed social networks may contain redundant social relations that obstruct precise user preference characterization for graph-based social recommendation.

gap.claim: Identifying and removing redundant social relations is challenging because labels are lacking.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Graph Bottlenecked Social Recommendation (GBSR), a model-agnostic framework for denoising social graphs for recommendation.

GBSR uses an information bottleneck objective that maximizes mutual information between the denoised social graph and recommendation labels while minimizing mutual information between the denoised social graph and the original graph.
GBSR combines preference-guided social graph refinement with HSIC-based bottleneck learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GBSR as a novel framework for addressing social noise in social recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments showing high performance and good generality when GBSR is combined with various backbones.
The authors report that code is available at the linked GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Social recommendation uses graph-based methods to capture high-order social influence.
Existing methods use observed social networks, but real-world networks may contain redundant relations and labels for denoising are unavailable.
The paper introduces GBSR, which learns a minimal yet sufficient denoised social structure through an information bottleneck perspective.
The framework includes preference-guided social graph refinement and HSIC-based bottleneck learning.
The authors report extensive experimental results across various backbones.

source_observation.claim: The framework seeks a social graph that retains information useful for recommendation while discarding information from the original graph.

interpretation.claim: Information bottleneck objectives can provide a label-free way to control redundancy in observed relational structure.

application.claim: For recommendation systems with noisy relation data, consider optimizing task-relevant information jointly with compression of the observed graph.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers to settings with different noise types, tasks, or graph semantics.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical experimental results are not specified.
The abstract does not describe the HSIC-based bottleneck learning objective in implementation detail.
The abstract does not quantify the amount of redundant social relations removed or the recommendation improvement.
